item.title: Grammar will meet Ra High in Deans semifinal
item.description: Suva Grammar School will meet Ra High School in the Vodafone Super Deans semifinal next week after beating Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute 23-7 this evening. The boys from Nasese ran in four tries, while Alfred Cornish scored Ba Pro's lone try.
item.content:encoded:
Suva Grammar School will meet Ra High School in the Vodafone Super Deans semifinal next week after beating Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute 23-7 this evening.

The boys from Nasese ran in four tries, while Alfred Cornish scored Ba Pro's lone try.

The Grammar forwards dominated the collision area before spreading the ball wide.

Ba Pro was eventually able to score in the second half taking advantage of the one man advantage as the Grammer centre was still in the sin bin through their flanker who broke two tackles before sprinting over 30 metres to score under the sticks.

With the last quarterfinal now being played, the semifinal fixtures are now confirmed with Nasinu Secondary School to play Lelean Memorial School next week.

In the games earlier today at Garvey Park, Tavua, Ra High caused an upset when they edged defending champions Ratu Kadavulevu School 12-10, while Nasinu defeated Cuvu High School 28-26.

At the HFC Bank Stadium, Lelean thumped Ratu Navula 26-5 in the first quarterfinal.

item.title: Assistant Sports Minister raises concerns over Garvey Park conditions
item.description: Concerns were raised earlier today on the conditions of Garvey Park in Tavua after students were digging out stones from the ground. Assistant Minister for Sports, Aliki Bia had raised the alarm saying this is not good and it does not portray a good image for the development of our rugby.
item.content:encoded:
Concerns were raised earlier today on the conditions of Garvey Park in Tavua after students were digging out stones from the ground.

Assistant Minister for Sports, Aliki Bia had raised the alarm saying this is not good and it does not portray a good image for the development of our rugby.

Bia says the welfare of students and players is paramount.

This is also because it is the first time that Garvey Park is hosting the Vodafone Super Deans National Quarterfinals as well as the Weetbix Raluve Quarterfinals.

Concerns have also been raised on how hard, and dusty the ground is with two players already being taken off the field in ambulances.

The U18 quarterfinals are currently underway at Garvey Park between Ra High School and Ratu Kadavulevu School, which will be followed by Cuvu College vs Nasinu Secondary School at 3.05pm.

At the HFC Bank Stadium, Lelean will play Rati Navula at 4.30pm, followed by Grammar and Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute at 5.55pm.

item.title: Months of sacrifice rewarded as young performers shine before full house in Sina premiere
item.description: Months of rehearsals, long days and little sleep turned into a night to remember for the young cast of Sina , who performed before a full house at the University of the South Pacific last night. The production marks Oceania Arts, Culture and Pacific Studies' first major performance since December 2023, and the official relaunch of its performing and musical arts programme.
item.content:encoded:
Months of rehearsals, long days and little sleep turned into a night to remember for the young cast of Sina , who performed before a full house at the University of the South Pacific last night.

The production marks Oceania Arts, Culture and Pacific Studies' first major performance since December 2023, and the official relaunch of its performing and musical arts programme.

Twenty-six-year-old Laisenia Qarase, who played the role of the eel, says he never imagined performing in front of such a large audience.

He says the cast often rehearsed from morning until late at night, with some members getting only a few hours of sleep before returning to training the next day.

Qarase says seeing every seat filled made all the hard work and sacrifices worthwhile.

He thanked the directors for believing in him and giving him the opportunity to take on one of the production's leading roles.

Qarase says he hopes theatre and performing arts will receive greater support in Fiji, adding that the country has no shortage of talented performers.

Eighteen-year-old Lina Daunakamakama, who played the lead role of Sina, says she was overwhelmed by the support shown by the audience.

She says she did not know what to expect before stepping onto the stage but was delighted to see a packed auditorium.

Daunakamakama says preparing for the production was challenging after it was postponed several times, but the extra time allowed the cast to refine their performance.

She says portraying Sina meant understanding the character's emotions and journey, something she found deeply personal.

Daunakamakama thanked the directors, her parents and fellow cast members for supporting her throughout the journey, saying they made the experience both memorable and rewarding.

item.title: I thought my life was over, but disability did not stop my dreams- Laisenia
item.description: Laisenia shared how he overcame discrimination to become an advocate for people with disabilities. Originally from Lakeba, with maternal links to Fulaga in Lau, Laisenia says he developed juvenile rheumatoid arthritis after an accident while in Class 6, leaving him unable to walk without assistance.
item.content:encoded:
Laisenia shared how he overcame discrimination to become an advocate for people with disabilities.

Originally from Lakeba, with maternal links to Fulaga in Lau, Laisenia says he developed juvenile rheumatoid arthritis after an accident while in Class 6, leaving him unable to walk without assistance.

He says the condition affected his joints and forced him to spend two years in hospital before facing another challenge when he returned to school.

Laisenia says the hardest part was not living with a disability but dealing with the attitudes of others.

He says there was little awareness of disability at the time, and after experiencing discrimination and negative attitudes, he eventually left school.

Laisenia later completed a Diploma in Information Technology and is now studying towards a Bachelor's degree while working with the National Council for Persons with Disabilities Fiji.

Drawing on his own experience, he says Fiji has made significant progress in recognising the rights of people with disabilities through new laws and policies, but more needs to be done to turn those commitments into real change.

Laisenia says disability is not the biggest barrier. Instead, he believes negative attitudes, inaccessible buildings, limited public transport and services that do not meet the needs of people with disabilities continue to prevent many people from reaching their full potential.

He is calling on the Government, schools and communities to improve awareness of disability rights from an early age and ensure children with disabilities are included in every part of society.

Laisenia says every child deserves the opportunity to learn, succeed and be treated with dignity, regardless of their disability.

item.title: Seaqaqa cane farmer calls for agricultural leases to be extended to 50 years
item.description: Seaqaqa sugarcane farmer Hamid Khan is calling on the Government to extend agricultural lease terms from 30 years to 50 years, saying the current lease period is too short for farmers to fully benefit from their investments. Khan made the submission to the Parliamentary Standing Committee during its public consultation at the Seaqaqa Hall.
item.content:encoded:
Seaqaqa sugarcane farmer Hamid Khan is calling on the Government to extend agricultural lease terms from 30 years to 50 years, saying the current lease period is too short for farmers to fully benefit from their investments.

Khan made the submission to the Parliamentary Standing Committee during its public consultation at the Seaqaqa Hall.

Khan says the 30-year lease term creates uncertainty for farmers because they are required to pay another lease premium when the lease expires.

Khan says by the time farmers have developed their farms, the lease is nearing its end and they are required to pay the lease premium again.

He says if leases are extended to 50 years, farmers will have greater confidence to plan ahead and invest in developing their sugarcane farms.

Khan also raised concerns about lease rental costs, saying he pays around $700 a year for his seven-acre farm, which he believes is too expensive.

He says sugarcane farmers are already burdened by rising production costs, including fertilisers, weedicides and labour, leaving them with very little profit.

Khan adds that despite previously raising concerns about reducing lease rental costs, no action has been taken.

He is now urging the Parliamentary Standing Committee to carefully consider the concerns of cane farmers and recommend reforms that will provide greater security and reduce financial pressure on those in the sugar industry.

item.title: Taveuni residents still waiting for water as shortage worsens
item.description: Residents in parts of Taveuni say the ongoing water shortage is becoming increasingly desperate, with some families still waiting for water despite reaching out to the Water Authority of Fiji for assistance. A resident from Naselesele told fijivillage News that after contacting WAF to arrange a water cart to fill his household tanks, he was asked to provide his details and was told someone would c
item.content:encoded:
Residents in parts of Taveuni say the ongoing water shortage is becoming increasingly desperate, with some families still waiting for water despite reaching out to the Water Authority of Fiji for assistance.

A resident from Naselesele told fijivillage News that after contacting WAF to arrange a water cart to fill his household tanks, he was asked to provide his details and was told someone would call him back with a quotation.

However, he says several days have passed and he has not received a phone call or an email.

The resident says the situation has become critical as families continue to struggle without a reliable water supply while the dry spell persists.

Last week, WAF told fijivillage News that prolonged dry weather had significantly reduced water levels at the Mua raw water source, affecting water production and supply to several communities across Taveuni.

The Authority says it was carrying out water rationing and valve operations to manage the limited supply, adding that normal water supply would only be restored once there is sustained rainfall and the island's raw water sources recover.

Questions sent by fijivillage News to the Ministry of Rural and Maritime Development and Disaster Management last week on what assistance is being provided to affected communities remain unanswered.

We have also sent further questions to the Water Authority of Fiji regarding the concerns raised by residents, including the reported delays in arranging water deliveries, and are awaiting a response.
